data.gender_notes: Sant is used as a masculine name in Hindu naming traditions.
data.long_meaning: A person who has achieved enlightenment through deep spiritual practice and self-discipline. The name Sant carries the meaning “Saint, holy” and is chosen by families in Hindu traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Hindu tradition and is also used in Sanskrit, Punjabi. Parents who choose Sant usually hope their child will grow to embody saint, holy and live with faith, good character and purpose.

data.etymology: Sant belongs to the Hindu linguistic tradition and is used in Hindu naming. Its recorded meaning is “Saint, holy.”
data.numerology_meaning: In Pythagorean numerology the letters of Sant total 9, giving a life-path number of 9. Number 9 is linked with Mars and with the qualities of compassion, idealism and generosity.

in_sanskrit.name: संत
in_sanskrit.meaning: A man of peace, a sage, or a saint.
in_sanskrit.long_meaning: Derived from the Sanskrit word संत (sant), which means 'one who is steadfast in his vows, a man of peace, a sage, or a saint.' In Hinduism, a Sant is a spiritual leader who has renounced worldly pleasures and is devoted to the pursuit of wisdom and self-realization.

in_hindi.name: संत
in_hindi.meaning: A person who is pure at heart, or a wise and virtuous person.
in_hindi.long_meaning: Derived from both the Sanskrit word संत (sant) and the Hindi word संत (sant). In Sanskrit, it means 'one who is steadfast in his vows, a man of peace, a sage, or a saint.' In Hindi, it can also mean 'a person who is pure at heart, or a wise and virtuous person.'

historical_references.reference: Sant Tukaram was a 17th century Marathi poet-saint from Maharashtra, India. He lived during the period of the Maratha Empire, from 1608 to 1649. He was a devotee of the Hindu god Vitthoba and is considered a saint in the Maharashtra tradition.
historical_references.context: Maratha Empire, Hindu god Vitthoba, Maharashtra tradition, poet-saint

historical_references.reference: Sant Ravidas was a 15th-century poet-saint from northern India. He was a member of the Valmiki caste, and is considered a saint in the Bhakti movement, a Hindu religious tradition that emphasizes devotion to a personal god. He lived during the period of the Delhi Sultanate, from 1450 to 1520.
historical_references.context: Delhi Sultanate, Hindu Bhakti movement, Valmiki caste, poet-saint

modern_usage.modern_context: The name 'Sant' originated from Hinduism, historically referring to a person who has renounced worldly life to pursue spiritual goals. However, in modern times, the term 'Sant' has evolved to encompass individuals who may not have renounced the world entirely but are deeply committed to personal growth, spiritual exploration, and self-realization. This modern context is seen on various platforms including social media, spiritual retreats, and therapeutic communities. On social media, individuals may identify as 'Sants' when using spiritual handles or engaging in online communities that promote mindfulness, meditation, and other spiritual practices. In spiritual retreats, the term 'Sant' may be used to describe leaders or guides who provide spiritual guidance and support to attendees seeking personal growth and enlightenment. In therapeutic communities, the term 'Sant' may be used to describe individuals who have undergone significant spiritual transformation and are now dedicated to helping others on their own spiritual journeys.
